predecessors.name: Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic
predecessors.text: the Transcaucasian federation of 22 April-26 May 1918, from which Georgia seceded

successors.name: Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic
successors.text: the whole of the Democratic Republic, occupied by the Red Army in February-March 1921

ledger.x: 1918, 26 May: Georgia declares independence at Tiflis.
1918, 7 December: the Georgian-Armenian War begins over Lori.
1919: Georgia takes over the Ottoman-held south (Akhaltsikhe, Akhalkalaki).
1920, end of the year: Georgia reoccupies the Lori neutral zone.
1921, March: the Democratic Republic ends and its land becomes the Georgian SSR.
1991, 9 April: Georgia declares independence from the Soviet Union (finalized 26 December 1991).
1992, 24 June: the Sochi Agreement ends the South Ossetian war.
1992, 14 August: Georgian forces enter Abkhazia and the war begins.
1993, 27 September: Sukhumi falls and the war ends.
1993, 27 September: Abkhazia passes to the Abkhaz.
2008, August: Russian forces occupy Georgian towns beyond the conflict zones.
2008, August: the Upper Kodori Gorge falls to the Abkhaz.
2008, 8 October: Russian forces leave the buffer areas.

wars.name: Georgian-Armenian War
wars.outcome: Ceasefire at midnight on 31 December 1918 after British and French intervention; a neutral zone follows, the final settlement left to the Paris Peace Conference.

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Georgia
wars.outcome: Soviet victory: Tbilisi falls on 25 February, the government leaves on 18 March; Turkey claims Ardahan and Artvin (ultimatum of 23 February) and drops its claim to Batumi (Treaty of Kars, 13 October 1921).

wars.name: Georgian-Ossetian conflict (South Ossetia War, 1991-1992)
wars.outcome: Sochi ceasefire of 24 June 1992; separatists keep Tskhinvali, Java, Znauri and parts of Akhalgori; Georgia keeps the Georgian villages and the rest of Akhalgori.

wars.name: Georgian Civil War (1991-1993)
wars.outcome: Zviad Gamsakhurdia, elected president on 26 May 1991, was 'soon deposed in a bloody coup d'etat, from 22 December 1991 to 6 January 1992'; 'a bitter civil war ... lasted until December 1993'.

wars.name: War in Abkhazia (1992-1993)
wars.outcome: Abkhaz victory: Sukhumi falls on 27 September 1993; 'Abkhazia becomes a de facto independent republic'; Georgia keeps the Upper Kodori Valley.

wars.name: Russo-Georgian War
wars.outcome: Russian victory: ceasefire negotiated by Sarkozy on 12 August; Russia recognises Abkhazia and South Ossetia on 26 August; Georgia loses Akhalgori and the Upper Kodori Gorge; Russian forces leave the buffer areas on 8 October 2008.
